title: Smaller Audio or More Even Volume? Choose the Right Compression
description: Choose between smaller audio files and more even listening levels. Learn which type of compression fits your recording and what to check on iPhone.
direct: If your attachment is too large, reduce its file size. If some parts are too quiet and others are too loud, use a tool that changes the volume differences.

cards.decision.heading: Start with the distinction
cards.decision.body: A lecture that will not fit in an upload needs a smaller encoded copy. A lecture whose speaker alternates between whispers and loud speech needs an audio-level editing workflow. Identify which obstacle you have before choosing a tool.
sections.detail-0.heading: Why a smaller file may sound just as uneven
sections.detail-0.body: MP3 and AAC encoding aim to represent audio using less data. Dynamic-range compression instead changes the relationship between louder and softer passages. Lowering an export bitrate does not establish that a distant speaker will become easier to hear. Conversely, applying a volume effect and saving an uncompressed WAV can leave a large attachment.
sections.detail-1.heading: Choose the next tool honestly
sections.detail-1.body: Its current listing offers file compression, conversion and trimming; it does not promise a mastering compressor or automatic loudness leveling. Export tools require Pro. If uneven volume is the actual obstacle, an editor with a documented compressor, such as Audacity, is the appropriate separate workflow. Make your small delivery copy after that editing is finished.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Should I compress file size before adjusting loudness?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: When possible, edit volume from the best source first. Make the smaller delivery copy after the edits so you can avoid another lossy encode.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why did reducing bitrate do nothing for the quiet speaker?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Bitrate controls how much data the saved audio uses. It does not target the difference between that speaker and louder parts of the recording.

steps.step-1.text: Keep the original recording. Check whether the problem is measured in megabytes, inconsistent listening volume, or both.
steps.step-2.text: For a smaller file on iPhone, open the recording in Audio Compressor MP3 Converter and use its compression or format-conversion tools. Choose an available export suitable for the receiving app.
steps.step-3.text: Save a separate copy, compare its actual file size, and listen to quiet speech and busy passages. Confirm playback in the destination before sending the complete recording.
